items.note: Association, organized 1889, Gideon Vose founder and first president (Story 1, Story 3). 1891 is missing, but the item has no REQUIRED line, so the core fact is enough.
Article VII (payment by butterfat by test, the station test governs) is not in Section A.
Absent: that payment by test is what made a wrong test cost money.
Loomis, Teague and Sill are not in Section A.
Section A says 'son of Gideon Vose' but gives no 1913. The sheet elsewhere asserts the planted value 1911 (B3, D3).
The station-gain ledger line is not in Section A.
Ostrey Hollow station, seven miles up the valley, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896. The borrowing of Larrow Green glass in Section A is not stated, but the core fact is present.
Weighed, sampled, tested; cream to Larrow Green, skim returned (Story 1); neck ruled for the full charge (Story 7).
Ammon & Sons, Tarnet; invoice 14 April 1897; in use 1 May 1897.
6 dozen pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., 12 dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93.
Story 3: 0.19, 'flat as a floor, in every month of the year', June flush and February alike. (The Hollow-vs-Green conflation is charged at A4.3.)
Absent: that a pipette cannot be checked without a burette and there was none in the county.
Twenty-nine seasons; dismissed 30 April 1925 (Story 5).
Bench routine and one-hand test book not described. Story 1 also wrongly gives Keddie a private weigh book.
Section A never gives the summary leaf's 1896 figure of 3.80 against 3.61 from 1898.
8 May to 10 July 1911, nine weeks, a rise of 0.19 over 3.61, a fall back on the return of the station's glass, and the question mark.
Married to Orra Brant, sister of Emmet Brant, the largest patron.
The 1919 circular is present, but Keddie's own 17 March 1925 statement ('tested as taught, cannot say why') is absent. Both are required.
Died 1934.
Hessel Bottom, six farms, Emmet Brant the largest patron.
Brant's weigh book is mentioned only as an exhibit; no 1 Jan 1897 start and no agreement of the two scales.
Gate failed: Story 3 gives Hollow 3.61 against Green 3.78 and calls the difference 0.19. C1(b) repeats it.
The 1908 committee is mentioned, but without Nyle Grigg or the January-March sampling.
Absent: Brant's 1910 year of 200,000 lb at 3.42, and the proportional loss.
Absent: the weigh book passing to Roy Brant and being lent to Ivy in 1958.
Only 'the cheese company over the ridge' in Vessey County. Alder Corners and Redlow Ridge are never named.
Absent: the four patrons hauling there in the summer flush from 1915.
Absent: the independence of the Alder Corners test.
Absent: 0.19 higher at Alder Corners over sixteen seasons.
Absent: same milk, different buildings, killing the hay and water explanations.
Story 7: Rosalie Cudd, Jerome Cudd's daughter and keeper of the family test book, supplied production records for Ivy's 1958 work.
Strawn is named as state inspector, but Section A dates his lactometer work 'from 1908 onward' (NT-23), not 1907-1936.
Lactometer on every circuit visit; never found added water.
Condemnation dated June 1922, not 12 June 1923.
States only that he 'drew no inference'. The bolded 'wrote no figure / no report beyond the condemnation' is absent.
Replacement ordered 28 June and acknowledged 2 July, but in 1922, and the 1924 average is given as 3.85 (planted error).
Crate to the loft is present; the notebooks going to the college library in 1947 is absent. Both are bolded.
Patrons petitioned January 1925.
Board sat 17 March - 4 May 1925, two of three sittings in the weigh room. The chairman is unnamed ('an attorney at Ashlin'), but the core fact is present.
Story 3 gives the three explanations (water/Vose, theft, bog hay), running to 1925: 'Three theories. None could stand.'
Four books named, but the inspector's notebook is 'for 1922', not 1923.
Dismissed 30 April 1925, 'the finding said nothing'; award 4 May 1925, $3,800 'without admission'.
No one-fifth of $19,000 (gives $19,600) and no charge to the station-gain account.
Granddaughter; State Agricultural College at Farland; graduate work under Leland Vaught.
The 'records never in the same room' assembly is not stated; only notebooks and Cudd records are mentioned.
February 1958, crate in the station loft, nine pipettes survived.
Gives 16.27 c.c. and 1.33 short (NT-1).
Gives 7.55 percent short, not 95 percent of true / 3.61 for 3.80.
67,000 lb and $19,600 (planted errors); no ledger identity.
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, clears him; 33 years after dismissal, 24 after death.
Granddaughter.
Duncan is Ivy's father and Ansel's son (r18), with r22's correction.
Second cousins, derived through Emmet/Orra as siblings and Roy/Duncan as first cousins.
Asserts they were half-siblings 'through their father's second marriage'; does not abstain.
Gideon Vose.
No link from Article VII (test decides pay) to Selby's accusation, and no Vose Jerseys largest-loser point. Discusses signing habits instead.
Headline verdict: 'No blood relationship existed between the Voses and the Keddies.'
Treats a family denial as carrying weight; never says no document names or denies a link.
States true average 3.80 and short 0.19. The final figures match, although they were reached by an additive route through the Green comparison.
Does not compute 6,840 lb; says the figure is not in the sources.
Gives a speculative $300, not $86.40.
1,444,000 lb credited.
74,630 lb, 5.17%/5.45%; wrong difference.
Items summed to $77.93, with $77.39 noted as a variant that the accounting refutes.
72 pipettes correct, but short by 1.33 c.c., not 0.88. Both are required.
Gives 25 years (May 1897-June 1922), not 26 years 6 weeks against 25 full years.
Abstention item A02: asserts a first-season figure (headline '11,100,000 pounds' from r23).
Variable: the pipette; one change of equipment.
Same tester, patrons/herds, season, pasture, machinery.
Says only 'rose markedly' and 'fell back'. No 3.80 through the interval or 3.61 on 10 July anywhere in B-G.
The cause is the glass, not skill, milk or cows. Limits: not by how much, not whether pipette or bottle.
Three reasons, but cited to only two narrators (r22 twice, r23). The ledger reason also misreads the gain as a loss.
Argues the reasons rest on different evidence (test book, lactometer, ledger) and names 1911 as holding without the 1958 measurement.
Abstention item A09: asserts 'Teague did not question the entries.'
Declines the literal question: 'The sources cannot determine whether Selby Vose consciously knew that the tests were systematically low.'
Only two of the five: ledger signatures and the 1919 circular. The manager year is wrong (1911); no hearing argument and no 'never names glass'.
Abstains (no deduction), but gives at most one supporting observation (signature vs reading); two are required.
Great-niece vs granddaughter resolved by the family record; glass in use 1897 vs r23's 1898 resolved by invoice and diary; $77.39 vs $77.93 resolved by arithmetic. None is noticed as a pair.
No real near-tie pair identified. The claimed pair (r19 great-niece / r21 first cousins once removed) carries different values.
A04, A06 and A10 not treated as abstention conflicts.
States 'None detected' for self-refutation.
Uses 16.27 c.c. and 7.55%, the end date 1922 and the 1924 average 3.85; no 0.19 = 5% of 3.80.
Watering named (Vose) and defeated by Strawn's lactometer readings.
Theft named and defeated by the 1911 interval under the same tester.
Bog hay named (1908 committee, vet) and defeated by Bulletin 214's 0.05 in winter and nothing in summer, against 0.19 in July.
Abstention item A07: headline 'No.'
Abstention item A05: 'Ansel Keddie believed something was wrong with the glass.'
Summary is roughly 250 words, over the 150 limit.
Record series are not named as such; fewer than five are identifiable.
Contains 67,000 lb and $19,600.
Only 1897 and 1958 are present. The condemnation is dated 1922, the error size and loss are wrong, and Ivy is not named.
